21	
22	Setting: Corrie Lane Outpatient Centre is one of two outpatient sites run by Hollins Vale Hospitals, a fictional regional hospital group. It runs orthopaedics, dermatology and endocrinology clinics, Monday to Friday, with about 2,900 appointments still booked on the day each month. On 3 March 2026 it moved from a legacy scheduler to Tidewell Scheduling, supplied by Osterline Systems. The sister site, Eastgate Outpatient Centre, is still on the legacy scheduler.
23	
24	Presenting request: The operations director asks why the did-not-attend (DNA) rate at Corrie Lane has gone from about 8% to over 13% since the scheduler change, and what the hospital should do about it. The board wants a recommendation by November.
25	
26	INITIAL EVIDENCE
27	E1 [stage S1] Email from Mairead Tolland, Director of Outpatient Operations, 9 Sept 2026 (leadership-account): Our did-not-attend (DNA) rate at Corrie Lane has gone from about 8% to over 13% since Tidewell went live on 3 March. The board wants an explanation and a fix by November. My view: the front desk stopped the day-before confirmation calls when the old system's printed call sheets went, and nobody told me. I'd like you to confirm that so I can deal with it through the team leads. Owen thinks it's partly the March cuts to the route 14 bus and partly that Tidewell 'counts differently'. Please tell us what is driving this and what we should do.
28	E2 [stage S1] Outpatient performance dashboard, Corrie Lane, extract 8 Sept 2026 (system-record): Monthly DNA rate (DNAs divided by appointments still booked on the day). Sep 2025 7.9%; Oct 8.3%; Nov 8.0%; Dec 8.7%; Jan 2026 7.6%; Feb 8.1% (mean 8.1%). Mar 2026: withheld; Apr 2026: withheld. May 13.1%; Jun 13.5%; Jul 13.6%; Aug 13.4% (mean 13.4%). Appointments booked on the day: 2,860–2,990 per month throughout. Footnote 1: March–April withheld until the outcomes of migrated appointments are reconciled. Footnote 2: according to the analytics team, month-to-month differences under 1 percentage point are normal variation at this volume.
29	E3 [stage S1] Change record CR-2026-0117, Tidewell go-live, Corrie Lane (change-record): Go-live 3 March 2026. All three specialties (orthopaedics, dermatology, endocrinology) switched over on the same day. Configuration: (1) Messaging. The legacy system sent one SMS 48 hours before each appointment. Tidewell sends a confirmation SMS at booking plus one reminder SMS at a fixed offset, set to 7 days (the vendor default). Tidewell allows one reminder offset per session template, and the vendor can change the offset for any template within two working days. (2) Booking. New and follow-up templates open 16 weeks ahead (legacy: 6 weeks). Follow-ups are booked at checkout instead of going on the recall list. (3) Outcome codes. The legacy code 'Arrived late – not seen' is mapped to Tidewell 'DNA'. Rollback: legacy system decommissioned 30 April.
30	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Bisi Adeyemi-Clarke, front-desk team lead, 12 Sept 2026 (staff-account): BA-C: 'We never stopped the calls. The day-before calls were always for the minor-procedures list, meaning skin ops and joint injections, so people know to stop blood thinners or arrange a lift home. Now I run that list from a Tidewell report instead of the old printout. What has changed is patients telling us at the desk that they didn't get "the text the day before" like they used to. And follow-ups now book their next appointment before they leave, sometimes four months out. Some of them look at the card and laugh.' Interviewer note: the director has asked BA-C to account for the call process, and she was visibly defensive.
31	E5 [stage S1] Patient Advice desk log, Corrie Lane, scheduling-related entries May–Aug 2026 (customer-account): Extracts (4 of 23 scheduling-related entries): (a) 'Used to get a text two days before. Now I get one a week before, and by the day I'd forgotten.' (b) 'Got a text the day I booked and one a week before, nothing nearer the time. Missed my endocrine review.' (c) 'Why are you texting me a week early? I nearly came on the wrong day.' (d) 'Was given an August date back in April. My shifts changed in the meantime and I couldn't get through on the phone to move it.' The other 19 entries: phone waiting times (11), car parking (5), other (3).
32	E6 [stage S1] Note from Owen Faraday, Clinic Manager, Corrie Lane, 10 Sept 2026 (manager-account): Honestly, I think a good chunk of this is Tidewell counting differently. The old system had a separate 'arrived late – not seen' code, and the migration lumped all of that into DNA. Until the data people sort out March and April, I'd suggest we stop sending the DNA figure to the board, because it makes us look worse than we are. The other thing is the bus. Vale Transit cut route 14 on 1 March, and a lot of our older patients rely on it.

52	H2: Longer booking lead times under Tidewell (16-week templates and follow-ups booked at checkout) are the main driver of the rise in missed appointments.
53	H3: The rise is mainly a recording artefact of Tidewell (for example, merging 'arrived late – not seen' into DNA); actual attendance has not materially fallen.
54	H4: External factors, either the 1 March route 14 bus service change or seasonal variation, account for most of the rise, independent of the scheduling change.
55	H5: Front-desk staff stopped or cut back the confirmation calls after go-live, and this explains the rise.

input.brief:
The rise in missed appointments is real and it comes from the Tidewell change. It is not the other things people suspected. Eastgate is on the old system and stayed at about 8%, so the bus cut and seasonal swings don't explain it. A clinical audit found miscoding accounts for only about 0.5 points of the 13.4%. Phone records show the day-before confirmation calls carried on at about 91–93% coverage, so the front desk didn't stop them. Written warnings would punish the wrong people. Hiding the DNA figure from the board would also be wrong.

Two things changed on the same day. The 48-hour text became a 7-day text, and booking lead times grew from about 19 to about 52 days. Both fit the data, and the patient comments point at both. Every specialty and appointment type rose, and we have no outcome data by lead time. So I can't say which one matters more, or whether it's both. I'm fairly sure of the exclusions and unsure about the split.

Next step: run the 8-week randomised test. Put the 48-hour reminder on half the templates, and ask the vendor for the appointment-level extract. Don't change the whole clinic's configuration yet. Keep reporting the DNA rate to the board, with a note that March and April are withheld.
